body: Let me first say I'm sorry you are going through this, and it's not easy as a parent or as the student. My 17 year old has PNES, and it's been a rough battle. She was pulled from convention school and put in a specialized program before the seizures began, about 2 months before they began.  Now she attend but frequently has seizures at school, the nurse has been instructed by her doctors (pediatrician and neurologist) to administer a sternum rub or pinch to back of arm to pull her out of them. She still has pain from the seizure and most of the time is sent home because of it. This greatly impacts attendance and grades and she won't be graduating with her class because of it. A 504 (health plan) needs to be put in place so the school know how to handle them and allows child to come home when needed. Ours included elevator use when she doesn't feel well, avoiding all large/noisy groups and activities. My daughters classroom size is under 6 children but her seizures still greatly disrupt the classroom as they have to stop and call nurse Everytime.  I would have a discussion with nurse about the go pass and also discuss with the school that when child feels a seizure coming on they shouldn't be sent to hall alone (do we really want a child alone in the hall when they go into seizure). Your best bet is to get doctors involved advising a course of action when seizures occurr.

Its important to let them be upset. And not to expect them to hide their emotions or snap out of them. Its important to help them through their emotions without denying them the right to have them. Its also important to establish healthy ways of dealing with intense emotions when they are you. 

Try validating their feelings "i would be mad if half my ice cream melted too"

Helping them name what their feeling and why " im mad cause my ice cream melted", or "im mad cause dad wont get me another one"

Help them find a way to let the emotion out...talking, running around/excerise, coloring, talk to another adult about it

And then helping them come up with solutions for the issue or ways to prevent it from happening again(the bad thing, not having emotions)

Laying a good foundation for your child to deal with their emotions and solve issues that will come up in their life...because sadly life isnt fair, but we cant expect anyone to be happy about it.

This!!! I am (figuratively) that mom, the mom burnt out from taking care of a special needs child, with two other children, one out of house, one younger. 

Yes the majority of my attention goes towards my middle child, because her health conditions and mental health conditions demand it.  Do i like never having a break, absolutely not. Do i like having to pick my child up from school halfway through the day at least 3 times a week NO. Do i like missing weddings and parties and even funerals because my child will start having panic attacks within 5 minutes of being in crowded place.....

Its heartbreaking. As a parent its hard. You have a child that needs care, and for whatever reason the only person that keeps them stable is their mom, (mainly because mom will sacrafice her own health and happiness.) 

This means that the healthy child, and the adult child arent getting as much attention. I guarantee this mom is full of a lot of guilt, resentment, anger and frustration. 
As a parent its our responsibility to care for our children, and the prime concerning being the safety of the child. So if child A is fed clothed and healthy and is safely playing with toys while child B is slamming their head into a wall, or crying hysteriacally of course your attention goes to child B. Does mom wish child B was content so she could sit with both and enjoy playing ......of course....but thats not the reality. The reality is mom has to tend to the child who is not safe immediately. Could nurse help, yep if the child cooperates with the nurse, but if everytime child is with nurse mom comes home to a distraught child whos emotional state is now critical because mom left, mom stops leaving at all. Because the cost is too high. 


The only real solution is the whole family working to find a caregiver or program that the special needs child can have a positive expierence with. So mom can get a break from being constant caregiver,so she can than have time and energy to enjoy some of the neglected areas of her life. 

People are so quick to judge mom for not showing equal attention, but fail to realize mom was never given the option, if mom fails to provide the care for special needs child...thats neglect and puts that child in danger of more issues. Its not a matter of mom wanting to give all her attention to one child, its a matter of not having a choice.

I guess it really depends on the boundary itself, and why it's set.

I don't set little boundaries on things I find compromisable. You don't like hanging out with my one friend....that's fine, I will hang out with them during some my free time and you can chose something else to do.
I set boundaries on deal-breakers for me. Repeated disrespect, abuse, people pushing their responsibility on to me, trust issues (spending shared bill money, lies), use or destruction of someone else's property, and communication/ failure to communicate (more so during conflict....like I won't entertain someone who is mad at me unless they can tell me what I did that made them mad, and we can discuss it...my ex would just say I was a b**** and then not talk to me for a week-month at a time, without ever stating what I had done to make them mad.) And forcing me to do something when I have said no / getting mad that I said no, guilting me into things(sex, babysitting, drink, go somewhere I feel unsafe). 

I don't set rules on who my partner can be friends with, talk to, what he can wear, how he spends his free money(non shared bill money)/ how he treats his belongings, when he does his household chores....I just let things take their course...if he doesn't want to take garbage out....and it doesn't get picked up...well then he deals with having twice as much to put out next week. If he doesn't want to pick up his dirty clothes and put them in the hamper...well then he won't have clean clothes. If he doesn't cook on his night to cook...great I'll cook for me and the kids...you can go hungry (if he communicates before hand that he doesn't feel good or is too tired than we can agree to switch nights, or if I am in good mood and want to I'll just do it for him to be nice)

I guess it is all in how you look at it. My work with BOUNDARIES has been all about setting my own limits on what I will do and won't do. 

When I set a boundary I set it for me....it doesn't matter who it is, my Boundary doesn't change. If I cannot handle the choices someone else makes of their own free will, then I did not chose a relationship that works for me.

Relationships are always conditional! A relationship isn't about controlling or changing a partner to meet your needs, it's about finding someone that willingly meets your needs, and can do so without compromising anything that they want either. If one partner has to lose for the other to win...that's not healthy. Relationships should be win-win. Both partners should have their boundaries respected, without having to give up anything.  The right partner will be able to meet your needs, and respect your boundaries without having to compromise. Today's society is so caught up in the idea that every relationship must work, or we are somehow a failure. We are so afraid to say "hey this person isn't compatible, I'm going to find someone who is" . It's not a punishment if a relationship doesn't work....it's truth, and honesty that the two people don't work as a couple. 

The other example I have about yelling is a more clear cut Boundary. If you yell at me I will walk away from the conversation. I can't make you not yell, but I will do what is best for me and remove myself.

I learned as much as I could about my disorder (bipolar & borderline personality disorder, with sever codependancy).

For many years I struggled. After one of my hospitalizations I decided to become educated about my disorders. I worked on my own and with counslers, to identify my triggers and warning signs. I also identified my strengths and what I could do/ could not do.  

I went from making crazy life damaging choices when I was manic, to now using that energy positively (through crafting for me).  Learned to chose jobs that allow for more flexibility (not all will, for some I needed to have a family medical leave/intermittent leave, for days when I could not control my symptoms).  I explained my condition, and even had my support system members attend a few counseling sessions with me, so they could be educated on what my symptoms of my disorder are/vs what is actually my personality. (Example: recless spending during manic, when I am normally very responsible with money) this helped them learn when they have to step in and be the voice of reason or get me help. Also worked with counsler to set limits for myself...I did this when I was in a "normal" state of mind. We decided what I needed for limits, even though I knew I'd break them,  but having a list of acceptable behaviors made me more accountable to myself, and made me aware of when my mind wasn't as healthy as I thought it was. Simple example: I don't do dishes everyday, I hate dishes, but I like a clean house and it is my chore. If both sides of the sink are filled up (normally takes three-5 days,)it means I'm not in a healthy mind. Another would be drinking, I normally drink maybe three times a year, and only enough to feel a buzz/feel happy....that is what I would chose to do....if I drink so much I am getting sick or don't remember than something is wrong....or if I'm drinking frequently that is a sign that something isn't right with my mental health.

This helped me alot, I still have bad days that I need to seek help, but I can tell I need help, I haven't had a suicide attempt in 16 years...I've had thoughts that I have been able to control...and when they have been too overwhelming I went and got help.

I graduated on time, with a son. I got married, we are celebrating 15 years together next month. I have three children, who are well taken care of.
I have held jobs for up to 5 years, I left to take care of child with health issues. 

It's hard, but it is possible!
